items.title: Section: Wanting Liberation and Still Flinching From It — Cessation's Confident Understanding

items.zh: 即於如是諸有、諸趣死生法中，以無願行、無所依行、深厭逆行發起勝解，精勤修習勝解作意。復於如是諸有、諸生增上意樂深心厭怖，及於涅槃隨起一行深心願樂。彼於長夜，其心愛樂世間色聲香味觸等，為諸色聲香味觸等滋長積集。由是因緣，雖於涅槃深心願樂，而復於彼不能趣入、不能證淨、不能安住、不能勝解，其心退轉。
items.en: Precisely within these states of existence, these destinies of death and rebirth, one gives rise to confident understanding through wishless conduct, conduct without reliance, and conduct of deep aversion, diligently cultivating this confident-understanding engagement … through the long night of time, the mind has taken delight in the world's forms, sounds, scents, tastes, and textures … for this reason, though one sincerely wishes for nirvāṇa, one is still unable to actually enter it, unable to attain purified conviction in it, unable to abide in it, unable to gain confident understanding of it — the mind keeps reverting back.

items.zh: 於寂靜界未能深心生希仰故，有疑慮故，其心數數厭離、驚怖。雖於一切苦、集二諦，數數深心厭離、驚怖，
items.en: Because one is not yet able to deeply admire and long for the realm of stillness, and because doubt remains, the mind again and again withdraws in aversion and alarm … at such a time, one gives rise to a thought like this: where, then, am I — my self — right now? This is what is called alarm.

items.zh: 及於涅槃數數發起深心願樂，然猶未能深心趣入。何以故？

items.title: Section: Spiritual Pride — The Subtlest Obstacle, Right at the Threshold of Insight

items.zh: 以彼猶有能障現觀麁品我慢隨入作意，間、無間轉。作是思惟：我於生死曾久流轉，我於生死，當復流轉；我於涅槃當能趣入，我為涅槃修諸善法；我能觀苦真實是苦，我能觀集真實是集，我能觀滅真實是滅，我能觀道真實是道；我能觀空真實是空，我觀無願真是無願，我觀無相真是無相；如是諸法是我所有。
items.en: Because there is still a coarse-grade conceit obstructing direct realisation, intruding into engagement now with a gap, now without one … one thinks thus: I have long circled through birth and death … I am able to observe suffering as truly suffering, I am able to observe origin as truly origin, I am able to observe cessation as truly cessation, I am able to observe the path as truly the path … all these things belong to me.

items.zh: 由是因緣，雖於涅槃深心願樂，然心於彼不能趣入。
彼既了知如是我慢是障礙已，便能速疾以慧通達。
items.en: Having recognised that this very conceit is an obstruction, one is quickly able to penetrate it with wisdom … having thus taken mind itself as the object observed by mind, with focused, unrelenting attention, one is able to prevent this coarse-grade conceit, which obstructs direct realisation by intruding into engagement, from arising at all.

items.title: The Path's Confident Understanding — Nothing Exists Outside the Mind That Perceives It

items.zh: 棄捨任運隨轉作意，制伏一切外所知境，趣入作意。
items.en: One relinquishes the habitually arising engagement, subdues every externally apprehended object, and enters into genuine engagement.

items.zh: 隨作意行，專精無間觀察聖諦；隨所生起心謝滅時，無間生心，作意觀察，方便流注，無有間斷。
items.en: Following this engagement, one observes the noble truths with focused, unbroken attention; the instant each arising thought passes away, without any gap a new thought arises to continue the observation — a skilful, flowing continuity, without interruption.

items.zh: 彼既如是以心緣心，專精無替，便能令彼隨入作意障礙現觀麁品我慢，無容得生。

items.title: Section: Watching the Mind Itself — All Four Truths in a Single, Compact Observation

items.zh: 如是勤修瑜伽行者，觀心相續，展轉別異，新新而生，或增或減，暫時而有，率爾現前，前後變易，是無常性。觀心相續，入取蘊攝，是為苦性。觀心相續，離第二法，是為空性。觀心相續，從眾緣生，不得自在，是無我性。
items.en: Thus, a practitioner diligently cultivating yogic discipline observes the mind's own continuity: ever shifting, ever distinct, arising newly moment after moment, now increasing, now diminishing, existing only momentarily, appearing suddenly, changing from before to after — this is its impermanent nature. Observing the mind's continuity as subsumed within the aggregates of grasping — this is its suffering nature. Observing the mind's continuity as apart from any second thing — this is its empty nature. Observing the mind's continuity as arisen from manifold conditions, ungoverning of itself — this is its selfless nature.

items.zh: 次復觀察此心相續，以愛為因、以愛為集、以愛為起、以愛為緣。如是名為悟入集諦。次復觀察此心相續所有擇滅，是永滅性、是永靜性、是永妙性、是永離性。如是名為悟入滅諦。
items.en: Next, one further observes this mind's continuity as having craving for its cause, craving for its accumulation, craving for its arising, craving for its condition — this is called entering into the truth of origin. Next, one further observes that this mind's continuity, once cut off by discerning wisdom, possesses a lasting extinction, a lasting stillness, a lasting sublimity, a lasting freedom — this is called entering into the truth of cessation.

items.zh: 次復觀察此心相續究竟對治趣滅之道，是真道性、是真如性、是真行性、是真出性。如是名為悟入道諦。如是先來未善觀察，今善作意方便觀察，以微妙慧，於四聖諦能正悟入。即於此慧親近、修習、多修習故，能緣所緣平等平等正智得生。由此生故，能斷障礙愛樂涅槃所有麁品現行我慢。又於涅槃深心願樂，速能趣入，心無退轉，離諸怖畏，攝受增上意樂適悅。如是行者，於諸聖諦，下忍所攝能緣所緣平等平等智生，是名為煗。中忍所攝能緣所緣平等平等智生，是名為頂。上忍所攝能緣所緣平等平等智生，名諦順忍。彼既如是斷能障礙麁品我慢，及於涅槃攝受增上意樂適悅，便能捨離後後觀心所有加行，住無加行無分別心。

blocks.text: The approach to the breakthrough: fear, then a subtle pride, then the mind watching itself. A passage (0475b28) is untranslated.

Within saṃsāra one cultivates understanding of cessation; but "because one is not yet able to deeply long for the realm of stillness, and because doubt remains, the mind again and again withdraws in alarm". One thinks: "Where, then, am I, my self, right now?" (Compare Day 173.) "Through the long night of time, the mind has delighted in the world's forms and sounds."

"A coarse-grade conceit obstructs direct realisation": "I have long circled through birth and death; I am able to observe suffering as truly suffering…" Recognising this conceit, "one is quickly able to penetrate it with wisdom", "taking mind itself as the object observed by mind".

"One relinquishes habitual engagement, subdues every externally apprehended object, and enters genuine engagement." Each thought, as it passes, is followed by a new one observing, "a flowing continuity".

subs.head: The four truths in the mind

blocks.text: The mind's continuity is "ever shifting, ever new, momentary": impermanent, suffering, empty, non-self. It has craving as its cause: origin. Cut off by wisdom, it can cease: cessation.

"Its counteracting path is truly path, truly the fitting way, truly practice, truly departure": the path. With this subtle wisdom, a knowledge arises in which knower and known are "equal". It removes the coarse conceit that obstructs the longing for nirvāṇa. At the lower grade of this knowledge one has **warmth**; middle grade, **summit**; upper grade, **forbearance in accord with the truths**. Then one lets go of all further effort and abides in a mind "without effort, without discrimination".

quiz.q: "Through the long night the mind has delighted in the world's forms, sounds …" What does Venerable Miào Jìng advise?
options: let no one mock another — everyone's been like this since beginningless time
quiz.why: "Through the long night of time, the mind has taken delight in the world's forms, sounds, scents, tastes, and textures." Venerable Miào Jìng: let no one laugh at anyone — since beginningless eons, it's been this way for all.

quiz.q: Conceit intrudes "with a gap, without a gap." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain?
options: "gap" refers to breaks in calm and insight; "no gap" refers to the conceit itself
quiz.why: "Because there is still a coarse-grade conceit obstructing direct realisation, intruding into engagement now with a gap, now without one." Venerable Miào Jìng: "gap" is said with respect to calm-and-insight practice having intervals; "no gap" is said with respect to the conceit itself.

quiz.q: "I am able to observe suffering … all these belong to me." What happens to long-time practitioners, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: veterans get short-tempered; beginners, feeling inadequate, stay humble
quiz.why: "I am able to observe suffering as truly suffering, I am able to observe origin as truly origin, I am able to observe cessation as truly cessation, I am able to observe the path as truly the path." Master Cháng Bǎi: old practitioners have big tempers, while new ones feel inadequate and are very humble.

quiz.q: "Mind observing mind, with focused, unrelenting (無替) attention." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain 替?
options: 替 means to cease — 無替 is unceasing
quiz.why: "Having thus taken mind itself as the object observed by mind, with focused, unrelenting attention, one is able to prevent this coarse-grade conceit … from arising at all." Venerable Miào Jìng: 替 means to abandon — so the sense is not stopping.

quiz.q: "Relinquishes the 任運隨轉 engagement" — rendered "the habitually arising engagement." How do the masters read it?
options: both: this engagement is the spontaneously arising conceit — the English misses it
quiz.why: "One relinquishes the habitually arising engagement, subdues every externally apprehended object, and enters into genuine engagement." Venerable Miào Jìng: this "spontaneously accompanying engagement" is the conceit. Master Cháng Bǎi: immediately relinquish the spontaneously arising conceit; once subdued, it no longer manifests. The English doesn't convey this.

quiz.q: "Observing the mind's continuity as apart from any second thing — this is its empty nature." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain "apart from any second thing"?
options: consciousness is the first thing, self the second — there is no self in consciousness
quiz.why: "Observing the mind's continuity as apart from any second thing — this is its empty nature." Venerable Miào Jìng: consciousness is the first thing and self the second; there's no self in consciousness — this is called emptiness.

quiz.q: "Observing the mind's continuity as subsumed within the aggregates of grasping." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain "aggregates of grasping"?
options: grasping is affliction, aggregates are the karmic result — the result arises from grasping
quiz.why: "Observing the mind's continuity as subsumed within the aggregates of grasping — this is its suffering nature." Venerable Miào Jìng: "grasping" is affliction, "aggregates" is karmic result; the result is born from grasping — hence "aggregates of grasping."
